topic: Do breakups really hurt like physical pain? (contested)
title: Do Breakups Hurt Like Physical Pain? It's Contested
voiceover: Do breakups really hurt like physical pain? In 2011, Ethan Kross and colleagues studied people who had recently had an unwanted breakup. Participants viewed a photo of their ex. They also felt physical heat pain in the scanner. Kross's team reported that activity overlapped in the secondary somatosensory cortex and the dorsal posterior insula during both experiences. In 2014, Choong-Wan Woo and colleagues tested this question again with 60 participants. They found separate brain patterns for physical pain and social rejection. So the two studies point in different directions. Both studies measured brain activity, not injury or damage, so neither shows a breakup physically harms the body. So breakups do activate pain-related areas, but whether that is the same as physical pain is still contested. Tomorrow: what is trauma bonding?

description: Does heartbreak overlap with physical pain in the brain? A 2011 study found overlapping activity in pain-related regions after a recent breakup, while a 2014 study with 60 participants found separate patterns for physical pain and social rejection. New psychology short every day on The Psyche Discourse. Source: Kross, E., Berman, M. G., Mischel, W., Smith, E. E., & Wager, T. D. (2011). Social rejection shares somatosensory representations with physical pain. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 108(15), 6270-6275. Source: Woo, C.-W., Koban, L., Kross, E., et al. (2014). Separate neural representations for physical pain and social rejection. Nature Communications, 5, 5380.
accuracy_note: Contested: the two studies reach different conclusions about overlap vs separate patterns. Both measure brain activity, not injury. The 'heat pain' detail in Kross et al. is from the study design as commonly summarized.
